26-qf3-bm-2592.solution: Expected winners = chance × players = 0.002 × 2,000 = 4. Everyone else is expected not to win, so 2,000 − 4 = 1,996.
26-qf3-bm-2592.trick: Winners are 0.002 × 2,000 = 4 (2 in every 1,000, and there are two thousands), so take 4 off 2,000 to get 1,996.

26-qf3-bm-2598.solution: The number of half-lives is 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Each half-life halves what is left, so the fraction remaining is (1/2)³ = 1/8.
26-qf3-bm-2598.trick: 9 hours is 3 half-lives, so halve three times: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8.

26-qf3-bm-2604.solution: In a regression line, the slope is the change in y for each one unit increase in x. A slope of 25 means y goes up by 25 units (on average) for every extra unit of x. So the answer is 25 units.
26-qf3-bm-2604.trick: No working needed: the slope already is the change in y per one unit of x, so just match the 25.

26-qf3-bm-2608.solution: Expected number = probability × total = 0.25 × 8,000 = 2,000. So 2,000 components are expected to be defective.

26-qf3-bm-2614.solution: A rotation of 180° about the origin sends (x, y) to (x cos 180° − y sin 180°, x sin 180° + y cos 180°) = (−x, −y). So (3, 4) goes to (−3, −4).
26-qf3-bm-2614.trick: A half turn flips both signs and keeps the sizes, so only (−3, −4) fits. The other two options change the sizes.

26-qf3-bm-2618.solution: An eigenvalue λ satisfies Iv = λv for some nonzero vector v. But Iv = v for every vector, so λ = 1. Also det(I − λI) = (1 − λ)ⁿ is zero only when λ = 1. So every eigenvalue of the identity matrix is 1.
26-qf3-bm-2618.trick: The identity leaves every vector unchanged, so its stretch factor is 1. That rules out 0 and −1.

26-qf3-bm-2622.solution: Distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). The gaps are 4 − (−2) = 6 and −1 − 3 = −4, so d = √(6² + 4²) = √(36 + 16) = √52. Since 52 = 4 × 13, the distance is 2√13.
26-qf3-bm-2622.trick: The gaps are 6 and 4. Take out the common 2: 2 × √(3² + 2²) = 2√13.

26-qf3-bm-2630.solution: Percentage increase = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. So (100 − 65) ÷ 65 × 100 = 35 ÷ 65 × 100 = 53.8%, which rounds to 54%.
26-qf3-bm-2630.trick: The rise is 35 out of 65, which cancels to 7/13, a little over a half. Only 54% fits: 35 is the rise itself and 65 is the starting value.

26-qf3-bm-2638.solution: A downward parabola peaks at t = −b ÷ 2a = −24 ÷ (2 × −4.5) = 24 ÷ 9 = 8/3. Then h = −4.5 × (8/3)² + 24 × (8/3) = −32 + 64 = 32. So the maximum height is 32 m.
26-qf3-bm-2638.trick: With no constant term, the top is b² ÷ (4a) using a = 4.5. That is 24² ÷ 18 = 24 × (24 ÷ 18) = 24 × 4/3 = 32.

26-qf3-bm-2644.solution: $36 is 36 × 100 = 3,600 cents, and one hour is 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds. So the rate is 3,600 cents ÷ 3,600 seconds = 1 cent per second.
26-qf3-bm-2644.trick: Dollars per hour ÷ 36 gives cents per second, because 100 cents over 3,600 seconds is 1/36. So 36 ÷ 36 = 1.

26-qf3-bm-2651.solution: The magnitude is √(p² + q²) = 25, so 7² + q² = 25². That gives q² = 625 − 49 = 576, so q = ±24.
26-qf3-bm-2651.trick: 7, 24, 25 is a standard right triangle triple (49 + 576 = 625), so q = ±24. Also 44 is bigger than 25, so it cannot work.
